about.title: Tehachapi Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Tehachapi is a mountain community of about 13,021 people, so when someone here dies because of another person's carelessness, the loss reaches neighbors, coworkers and congregations, not just one household. For 2025, the city's public records list 24 injury collisions and 35 people hurt, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. A wrongful death claim is not only about the road, though. Families may have a case after a fatal crash on Tucker Road or along W or E Tehachapi Boulevard, but just as often after a workplace accident, an unsafe property, a defective product or negligent medical care. California law gives a spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring the claim, followed by certain dependents and heirs, and it generally allows two years from the date of death to file. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match Kern County families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so you can ask your questions without adding another bill to everything you are already carrying.

whyChoose.title: Why Tehachapi Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out quickly whether you or another relative should bring the claim so the family moves together.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is much shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Connecting early keeps those dates from slipping by while you grieve.

items.title: Every category of loss counted
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Tehachapi recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death cases are rare here?
items.answer: Fatal crashes are only one source of these claims, and a quiet year on Tucker Road or Valley Boulevard says nothing about deaths that happen at work, in a care facility, or on someone else's property. Kern County families also lose relatives in collisions outside city limits, on the highway to Bakersfield or the Antelope Valley. If someone else's negligence played a part, it is worth a conversation regardless of where it happened.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash is facing criminal charges. Can we still bring a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death case is a civil action that runs separately from anything the Kern County District Attorney does. The criminal case can end in a plea or acquittal without affecting your right to seek compensation, and the civil case uses a lower standard of proof. Many families pursue both at the same time.

items.question: What if a city or county vehicle or a public road condition was involved?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow a different and much shorter timeline than the usual two years, often requiring a formal claim within months of the death. Missing that step can end the case before it begins. An attorney can tell you whether a public agency is a potential defendant and what has to be filed first.
